_comment: PROPOSED wire shape for closure captures -- NOT emitted by the producer yet. Source is the three cases below; every node is hand-written to chalk's requested contract so the disagreement surfaces on one sample rather than five CVs.
_source: my $n=5; my $get = sub { $n + 1 };  my $c=0; my $inc = sub { $c = $c + 1 }; my $rd = sub { $c };  print $get->(), $inc->(), $rd->();
_oracle: perl prints 611. ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: $rd->() is 1 because $inc->() already ran and its CellWrite is visible. Calling the three again prints 622 -- $inc mutates per call. A design that snapshots the value at capture time gives 610 on the first line and 610 again on the second, which is the failure this sample exists to catch.

nodes._case: 1. READ-ONLY capture. captured_written=false lets chalk skip the cell entirely and pass the value.
2+3. WRITTEN and SHARED. One cell, two AnonSubs take the SAME reference (#5) on their inputs.

main::__PROGRAM__::__ANON__:3:11._comment: sub { $n + 1 } -- read-only. The cell arrives as a CellParam -- a DISTINCT node kind, not Parameter with a flag: a capture is not positional, comes from no argument list, and has no declared index. A consumer that has not learned about captures GAPs on an unknown op rather than silently treating a cell as argument 0.; CellRead is on the memory chain even here, because whether it CAN be elided is chalk's call, not the producer's.

main::__PROGRAM__::__ANON__:5:11._comment: sub { $c = $c + 1 } -- reads THEN writes the same cell. CellWrite yields a new memory version (#6), which is what makes the sharing visible to the other closure and to the outer scope.

main::__PROGRAM__::__ANON__:6:10._comment: sub { $c } -- SAME cell as the one above. Its CellRead must observe the other closure's CellWrite; that is the case a value-on-inputs design gets wrong.
